name: NOV Inc.

profile.description: NOV Inc. designs, manufactures, and sells equipment and technology used in oil and gas drilling and production operations worldwide. Operates through two segments: Energy Equipment (rig systems, marine and offshore equipment, wellbore technologies) and Energy Products and Services (completion tools, tubulars, fiberglass systems, process and flow technologies). Expanding into low-carbon solutions including electrified drilling rigs, offshore wind installation vessels, and carbon capture technology. Q2 2026 Energy Equipment revenue of $1.19B (+4% YoY) and Energy Products revenue of $974M (-5% YoY), with capital backlog of $4.08B [1].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): NOV has incrementally expanded beyond traditional oilfield equipment into low-carbon solutions generating $339M in revenue in 2024, including electrified drilling rigs, offshore wind installation vessels, and carbon capture technologies [1][2]. This represents a meaningful new revenue stream but is evolutionary rather than transformative — the core business model remains oilfield equipment manufacturing serving the cyclical upstream energy industry. AI Deployment (1/2): NOV deploys machine learning and predictive analytics through its industrial data platform, with the Max Completion remote monitoring tool serving 3,500+ active users [2]. Collaboration with Armada on AI-powered edge devices for rugged industrial sites like offshore rigs. AI deployed in operations but specific revenue or cost savings not separately quantified. Market Share (1/2): NOV is a top-tier oilfield equipment manufacturer with leading positions in rig systems, drill pipe, and subsea flexible pipe, but operates in a fragmented, cyclical industry without dominant category-defining share [1]. Product Pipeline (1/2): Expanding pipeline in electrified rigs, offshore wind, and carbon capture technology. Q2 2026 orders included subsea flexible pipe awards in Brazil/Europe and North Sea rig reactivation, but next-gen product timelines remain vague [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): R&D spending at or near industry average for oilfield services equipment manufacturers.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): NOV's stated purpose centers on 'powering the industry that powers the world' and enabling safe, efficient energy production. Generic and interchangeable with any major oilfield services company — the mission describes what NOV does without articulating a deeper purpose or future state beyond serving the energy industry [2]. Community Impact (0/2): Standard corporate sustainability programs and HSE initiatives following SASB reporting standards. NOV's sustainability report describes itself as an 'equipment and technology provider' with limited direct environmental footprint, but no distinctive charitable programs or community investment with specific dollar amounts identified [3]. Employee Retention (1/2): Leadership transition from Clay Williams (retiring) to Jose Bayardo (new CEO effective January 2026) was orderly and well-planned, with Bayardo promoted from within after serving as COO and CFO over 15+ years at NOV [2]. Average retention indicators for the oilfield services sector without standout data. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful net insider buying in the last 12 months. CEO transition period with routine insider transactions.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Dividend stock with strong balance sheet and dividend history offset by depressed profitability from 2025 one-time charges. D/E of 37.3% scores perfectly at 1.0, reflecting NOV's conservative capital structure with $2.34B total debt against $6.27B equity and $1.55B cash [1]. ROE of 2.2% scores 0.15, significantly below the 15% target as FY2025 GAAP net income of $139M was depressed by substantial impairment charges (FY2025 EPS $0.39 vs $1.60 in FY2024 and $2.50 in FY2023). Revenue growth YoY of -1.4% scores 0.62 as FY2025 revenue of $8.74B declined slightly from $8.87B in FY2024 [1]. Revenue 5yr CAGR of approximately 7.5% scores 0.83. Forward P/E of approximately 20 scores 1.0, at the target level reflecting compressed expectations [1]. Profit margin of 1.6% scores 0.08, again depressed by one-time charges (FY2024 margin was 6.4%). Dividend metrics benefit from long payment history: 17+ consecutive years paid (score 1.0, 2x weight), 2 consecutive years of growth (score 0.2) after the 2020 dividend reduction, unsustainable GAAP payout ratio of 131% (score 0.0), and 5-year dividend growth CAGR of 58.5% (score 1.0, 2x weight) inflated by the low 2020 base. Liquidity floor cleared: 3.35M avg volume × $19.27 = $64.5M daily.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): NOV manufactures physical drilling equipment — rig systems, drill pipe, subsea flexible pipe, valves, and completion tools — deployed in extreme environments including deep water, high pressure, and hostile offshore conditions [1]. This deeply physical manufacturing and field service business is structurally immune to AI substitution. AI cannot fabricate a 30,000-foot drill string, assemble a semi-submersible rig, or deploy subsea equipment in 10,000 feet of water. Regulatory requirements (API standards, BSEE compliance) add additional moats that AI cannot circumvent. AI-driven drilling optimization may actually increase demand for NOV's monitoring and predictive analytics services as operators seek to optimize equipment utilization and reduce downtime. AI Opportunity (0/1): NOV deploys ML-based predictive analytics internally through its industrial data platform and the Max Completion tool (3,500+ users), and is collaborating with Armada on AI-powered edge devices for industrial sites [2]. However, these do not generate separately quantifiable AI revenue — AI enhances existing services rather than creating new revenue streams.

infinite_game.summary: NOV operates with a primarily finite-game mindset, focused on quarterly execution and shareholder returns through buybacks and dividends rather than pursuing a transformative purpose. The company is beginning to evolve toward energy transition products ($339M in low-carbon solutions), but the Just Cause is weak, competitive behavior is market-share focused, and the organizational culture lacks evidence of the deep trust and purpose-driven decision-making that characterize infinite players. The orderly CEO succession from Williams to Bayardo demonstrates planning but not vision [1][2].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): NOV's purpose of serving the energy industry with equipment and technology is functional rather than inspirational. The expansion into low-carbon solutions ($339M in 2024 revenue from electrified rigs, offshore wind, carbon capture) suggests an evolving sense of purpose beyond fossil fuels, but this is commercially motivated rather than cause-driven [1][2]. Leadership doesn't reference a higher purpose in strategic decisions — earnings commentary focuses on margins, buybacks, and operational excellence rather than advancing a vision of a better energy future.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): The leadership transition from Clay Williams to Jose Bayardo was orderly, with Bayardo promoted from within after 15+ years at NOV (CFO then COO), demonstrating leadership continuity and internal development [2]. The 35,000-employee organization operates across global manufacturing sites with adequate stability. No major layoffs or organizational disruptions identified. However, no specific voluntary turnover data, employee satisfaction metrics, or evidence of exceptional psychological safety distinguish NOV from industry norms.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): NOV operates in the oilfield services market with a traditional competitive mindset focused on market share and order capture. Competitive language in earnings calls centers on winning contracts, pricing advantage, and backlog metrics rather than learning from rivals' strengths [1]. No evidence of management citing competitors like Baker Hughes, Halliburton, or TechnipFMC as worthy rivals whose strengths reveal NOV's own weaknesses.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): NOV has incrementally evolved from a pure oilfield equipment company to include energy transition products — electrified drilling rigs, offshore wind installation vessels, and carbon capture technology generating $339M in 2024 revenue [1]. The Armada AI edge collaboration represents early-stage digital diversification. This is meaningful but represents incremental evolution within adjacent markets, not the transformative reinvention Sinek describes. The company has not fundamentally abandoned its core oilfield business to pursue the energy transition — it is adding to the existing model.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): The investment in low-carbon solutions while core oilfield revenue remains the primary business shows some willingness to invest in long-term capability [1]. The orderly CEO succession from Williams to Bayardo demonstrates succession planning. However, NOV's primary capital allocation strategy — share buybacks and maintaining dividends despite a 131% GAAP payout ratio on depressed earnings — reflects a focus on near-term shareholder returns over transformative long-term investment. The energy transition portfolio remains a small fraction of total revenue.

investment_thesis: NOV at $19.27 with a $6.87B market cap offers deep value characteristics with a forward P/E of approximately 20, conservative 37.3% D/E ratio, and $4.08B capital equipment backlog providing revenue visibility [1]. Q2 2026 demonstrated margin resilience with Energy Equipment revenue of $1.19B (+4% YoY) and improving product mix despite challenging end-market conditions. The 2.49% dividend yield with 17+ consecutive years of payments provides income while waiting for the oilfield cycle to recover. The low-carbon solutions portfolio ($339M in 2024) positions NOV for secular demand growth in offshore wind and carbon capture [2]. Share buybacks at compressed multiples create value for remaining shareholders, and the $1.55B cash balance provides a financial cushion against cyclical downturns.
thesis_continued: The primary bear case is cyclical revenue stagnation and deteriorating profitability. FY2025 revenue of $8.74B declined 1.4% YoY, and GAAP EPS collapsed from $1.60 to $0.39 due to significant impairment charges, reflecting the challenging industry environment [1]. The capital equipment backlog declined from $4.34B (year-end 2025) to $4.08B (Q2 2026), with management expecting full-year 2026 book-to-bill near only 100% — insufficient to rebuild backlog [1]. Q2 Energy Products revenue fell 5% YoY as lower global drilling activity and Middle East disruptions weighed on demand. The 131% GAAP payout ratio is unsustainable if earnings don't recover to normalized levels, and the dividend growth CAGR is inflated by the depressed 2020 base year following a 75% dividend cut. NOV remains deeply exposed to oil price cyclicality and the secular decline thesis for fossil fuel demand, with low-carbon solutions still representing less than 4% of total revenue. The new CEO Bayardo has yet to articulate a distinctive strategic vision.
key_catalysts: Energy Equipment segment showing resilience with Q2 2026 revenue of $1.19B (+4% YoY) driven by offshore production projects and favorable sales mix, with backlog of $4.08B providing multi-quarter revenue visibility [1]
Energy transition revenue growth from $339M in 2024 toward $500M+ as electrified drilling rigs, offshore wind installation vessels, and carbon capture technology capture secular demand tailwinds [2]

Deep value characteristics at forward P/E of ~20 with conservative 37.3% D/E, $1.55B cash, and 2.49% yield suggest limited downside at current levels; any oilfield cycle recovery would drive meaningful earnings expansion from the depressed base [1]
key_risks: Capital equipment backlog declining from $4.34B to $4.08B with book-to-bill expected near only 100% for 2026 — insufficient order momentum to rebuild backlog signals potential revenue erosion into 2027 [1]

FY2025 GAAP EPS collapsed 75.6% to $0.39 from $1.60 due to impairment charges, with profit margin of just 1.6% indicating the business generates inadequate returns; the 131% GAAP payout ratio is unsustainable without earnings recovery

Secular decline risk for oilfield services demand as global energy transition accelerates — NOV's low-carbon solutions ($339M) represent less than 4% of $8.74B total revenue, insufficient to offset a structural decline in fossil fuel capital spending [2]

backlog.note: Capital equipment backlog of $4.08B at Q2 2026, down from $4.34B at year-end 2025 and $4.30B at Q2 2025. Q2 2026 capital orders of $474M (+$54M YoY). Management expects full-year 2026 book-to-bill near 100%. Offshore production projects and subsea flexible pipe awards in Brazil/Europe provide backlog stability.
